label: Timpani, sampled, close and dry
audition_title: libsonare timpani vs the sampled reference
_notes: Every fourth semitone from 36 to 52, which is the range a set of drums is tuned across rather than a keyboard compass. Both ends and two points between were rendered before this definition was written; all are healthy, the pitch tracks the key throughout (65.8, 87.5, 131.7 and 175.8 Hz at notes 36, 41, 48 and 53), and the level is level -- the peak varies by 0.8 dB across the whole range, which is a drum being struck the same way rather than a sample being stretched.
_velocities: Five, matching the slots of this rack captured earlier so that one axis covers the whole of it. The axis is live on all four of these, at 15.5 to 31.7 dB between velocity 16 and 100, so none needed the exclusion a flat velocity response would have forced.
_dry: Nothing to switch off, measured rather than assumed: with the rack loaded not one of the plugin's 1526 advertised parameters matches `reverb` or `delay`, so `dry` has no section to act on and is left off rather than claiming an effect was disabled. What the recording contains is answered by `room`, which is a different question.
_room: No room, and the answer has to be declared because no note-tail measurement can reach it: a release and a small hall are the same falling signal over the tail a capture records, and the per-note agreement test that separates a room from one note's decay passes on a release perfectly. Three independent readings say there is none here. `calibrate` measures RT60 0.00 s; with the rack loaded not one of the 1526 parameters the plugin advertises matches `reverb`, `delay` or `room`; and the pizzicato at slot 14 settles it on its own -- it reaches digital silence 450 ms after the string is plucked, inside a four-second gate, which no space permits.
_stimulus: Two and a half seconds, sized to the longest ring in the grid. What the compass changes on this voice is how long it sounds: the note takes about two seconds to fall away at the bottom of the range and under one at the top, and the gate holds the longest of them whole.
_calibration: From `capture.py calibrate` on this rack, which its already-captured siblings were recorded against and whose settings this capture adopts so the slots of one rack stay comparable: a two-second settle against a measured minimum of 250 ms, and real time kept on although the reference renders the same either way, because a note streamed late is caught only by `verify` and would otherwise be committed as a measurement. What the recipe reports as non-determinism is worth stating precisely, because it is not round robin and a capture that recorded it as one would put a floor under the loss for nothing: two renders of the same cell correlate at 1.00000000 and peak within a thousandth of a decibel, differing only at -89 to -91 dB relative to the signal. That is one take rendered twice, not a second sample. The check is bit-identity, which is stricter than the question being asked.
_timbres: One, and the ladder is monotone above it, so this capture cannot move the voice past `voiced` however complete its coverage. That is a property of the source rather than of the work: the rack holds one slot per GM program, so there is no second timpani in it to disagree with, and `source_for` takes every timbre of a capture from one plugin, so a soundfont render cannot stand in as a second. What the reference does buy is the thing there was none of before -- a measured target for `autofit` and `--diagnose`, in place of voicing this program by ear. A second timbre needs a rack authored with an alternative in it, and this capture is written so that adding one is an edit to this list rather than a re-capture.
_dimensions: 10 of the 12 a modal voice can be judged on. `tnr` is kept and earns it: this is a strongly pitched drum, carrying 93 to 98 per cent of its energy within two per cent of the harmonics of the note struck, which is what a tuned kettle does and what separates it from every other percussion voice in the bank.
_dimensions_na: The exclusions as data, since a dimension argued only in prose reads as a gap.

dimensions_na.stereo: the slot renders dual mono: the two channels are bit-identical sample for sample, so the width is zero by construction rather than by voicing
dimensions_na.damper: note-off cannot be observed on this voice: the note has reached silence by about two seconds inside a 2.5 s gate, so the render is already quiet when the damper would act and there is nothing left for it to act on. The gate is left long enough to hold the whole free decay rather than shortened to make the release visible, because the decay is the measurement and the release would only be the gate's own edge

_identity: Which product this is captured from lives in the untracked sibling `timpani.local.json`: the plugin's component triple and the slot's preset. Everything here is the method. Re-capturing needs the overlay; scoring, fitting and diagnosing read `reference/timpani.json` and need nothing.
_slots: Slot identity is measured, never taken from a name or a position, and on this rack it is checkable against the repository's own committed measurements rather than argued from a spectrum: nine of its sixteen slots were captured in an earlier round. Rendered under each of those captures' own gates at a cell its profile holds, slot 6 returns a peak of -13.19 dBFS against a committed -13.19, slot 12 returns -16.52 against -16.52 and slot 15 returns -14.78 against -14.78. Three exact agreements fix slot n as GM program 31+n with nothing left to interpret. This slot: read off the confirmed numbering, with the measurement that does set it apart recorded beside it: its peak level is the same at every tuning, varying 0.73 dB from note 36 to note 53 while the note it sounds nearly triples. Every keyboard-mapped voice on this rack changes level across its compass by several times that. A set of drums struck the same way at each tuning is what that reads as, and it is what a timpani is. Two things that look like identifications here are not: the energy does follow the key rather than sitting at a fixed bowl resonance, 122 Hz at note 36 to 260 at note 53, so there is no fixed formant to point at -- the fixed figure a sustain-window reading gives is measuring the tail of a decayed drum rather than the stroke; and being low, pitched and decaying does not separate it from the eight basses on the same rack, which are all three.
